sections.text: If your search for “juke harris” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.text: If your search for “ncsa profile” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.text: If your search for “cedric taylor” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.text: If your search for “basketball analytics” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.text: If your search for “kylen thomas” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.text: If your search for “dejour reaves” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?

No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?

sections.text: If your search for “jeremiah anderson” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.text: If your search for “isaiah nelson” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.text: If your search for “kingston basketball” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.text: If your search for “maurice thomas” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?

Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.heading: Prepare your own basketball clip
sections.text: If your search for “tristan comer” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.text: If your search for “carter burgess” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?

What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.text: If your search for “miles hill” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

sections.text: If your search for “bryce owings” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.heading: Prepare your own basketball clip
sections.text: If your search for “donavan moore” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

sections.text: If your search for “jeremiah e burke” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?

What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.text: If your search for “mason keller” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.text: If your search for “ramone woods” is part of preparing your own basketball footage, start with a saved recording you own or have permission to edit. Select one continuous shot, preview a visible trail and keep the original alongside the exported copy. This page does not supply footage or claim any affiliation.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

subsections.heading: Bring a local video file
subsections.text: Choose a saved recording you own or may edit. A search result or share URL is not a video file and does not grant access to the recording.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut
subsections.text: A cut, sudden zoom or blocked ball can make the trail harder to review. Work on one clear shot before combining it with other plays in your usual editor.

sections.heading: Preview and export the traced basketball shot
sections.text: Select your saved file in the uploader, choose up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Review the release and arrival at the rim. When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and keep the edited copy alongside the source.

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.

faq: Can I paste a Hudl URL into HoopCut?
No. Select a video file saved on your device. HoopCut does not import Hudl URLs or access your account.
What if I cannot download the original clip?
Use the official Hudl help links and check the permissions available to your account. Ask the recording owner or coach for a copy you may edit. A share or embed link does not grant file access.
Is downloading from Hudl always free?
Do not assume so. Download availability and any cost depend on the Hudl product, account and video. The free Firework export offered here applies to the HoopCut effect, not Hudl downloads.
Will this tool upload the finished video to Hudl?
No. Save the traced file and manage any subsequent upload through your own authorized account.
Is the demonstration my team video?
No. It is a shared HoopCut example. Upload your own basketball clip to preview the effect on your footage.

sections.heading: Choose the part of the basketball clip worth tracing
sections.text: Keep one continuous attempt with the release, ball flight and rim visible. For a catch-and-shoot highlight, start before the pass arrives. For a pull-up, preserve the final dribble. End after the ball reaches the basket rather than cutting away during the flight.

subsections.heading: Avoid tracing across a montage cut

subsections.heading: Keep the effect separate from performance evidence
subsections.text: A tracer is a visual effect, not a shooting percentage, recruiting evaluation or measured ball trajectory. Preserve the original recording if a coach needs to review the unedited possession.
